formula: y_ip = P_p{ integral dt w_i(t) integral dlambda R_p(lambda) integral_Omega+ dOmega A(lambda,Omega) H(Omega) cos(theta) [L_tw(lambda,Omega,t) + L_bg(lambda,Omega,t)] } + r_dark_ip
quantity: downwelling hemispheric spectral irradiance via a horizontal diffuser (white board), NOT zenith radiance

w_i.text: exposure-weighting boxcars over the record's exposure window; equal-length repeats carry a_ij = 1/N

R_p.text: spectral channel kernel; published 1 nm grid suggests but does not prove a ~1 nm triangular response; the slit function was not measured. Unit convention: kernels are normalised to unit transmission so band integrals keep spectral-density units (W m-2 nm-1); band-integral quantities use the trapezoidal band integral explicitly
R_p.reason: line-spread function not published; band integrals on the published grid assume unit-transmission channels

A.text: white-board angular/horizontal correction relative to an ideal cosine receiver
A.reason: no measured angular-response curve is public; A=1 is the idealisation, not a measurement

H.text: horizon visibility (terrain/obstruction mask above the board)
H.reason: site horizon not characterised; H=1 is the idealisation

P_publish.text: publishing steps that apply to already-calibrated physical spectra (W m-2 nm-1 in and out): resampling onto the 1 nm published grid, the published median filter span 8 - which the upstream chain applies in the detector-response domain, i.e. E -> D*median(E/D) with D = correction_factor*pi from the vendored extract (filtering and a wavelength-dependent scaling do not commute; filtering E directly would reshape spectra by up to a few percent) - and the negative-value clamp. Implemented in publish_pipeline(); a model spectrum in physical units passes through these and only these steps before band comparison

C_capture.text: the raw-count-to-physical calibration chain (dark subtraction by nearest integration-time node and temperature interpolation, division by integration time in microseconds, sensitivity correction factor, pi factor). Defined ONLY on detector counts; it is replayed per record in replay.json to prove the raw/published binding. Applying C_capture to a model's physical irradiance would double-calibrate and must never happen

L_bg.text: astronomical + artificial night background; distinct from instrument dark residual r_dark

r_dark.text: residual instrument dark signal after upstream dark subtraction
r_dark.reason: dark handling is upstream (GetDarkSpectrum by integration time + board temperature); residual not independently measured here

units.published_spectra: W m-2 nm-1 (spectral density, as published)
units.band_integrals: W m-2 (per band, trapezoidal on the published grid)
units.cos_theta: applied once, inside the hemisphere integral
units.operator_domain: the formula integrates PHYSICAL radiance; only P_publish applies to its output. C_capture lives on the detector-count side of replay.json and is documentation of the upstream pipeline, not a model-facing step

forbidden_comparisons: hemispheric irradiance vs zenith radiance (different quantity)
published spectra vs model spectra without integrating model radiance over the hemisphere and the exposure window
treating night-spectrum medians as a measured background subtraction
applying C_capture (dark counts, sensitivity correction factor, pi) to a model's physical irradiance - that chain is defined on detector counts only and would double-calibrate
scenario_policy: response/horizon/background scenarios demonstrate dependence; they are not confidence intervals
